rules.rationale: allocator configuration clamps accepted bounds without eagerly reserving the cache ceiling and each new allocator snapshots the configured limits
allocator leases preserve chunk shape, bounded allocation-time ownership, reset reuse, column width admission, alias deduplication, borrowed-column rejection and stale-generation safety
empty, hook-once and synchronized allocator adapters preserve allocation shape, reuse admission, delegation and concurrent safety
Go testing.B entrypoints and b.N driver loops measure the preserved workload but are not observable TiDB package behavior.
The b.N timing loop is owned by the Go benchmark driver; deterministic setup and result-producing work remain covered.
Deterministic benchmark workloads preserve codec byte and row results; Go benchmark-runner timing is not a TiDB result.
Incremental decoding rounds bitmap batches, preserves fixed and variable values, tracks remaining rows, and reuses the final owner with rebased offsets.
Literal positive initialization and test bounds, plus testing.B positive iteration counts, make these zero-iteration companion paths unreachable.
Rust uses safe typed storage instead of Go unsafe slice reinterpretation and static bitmap initialization; emitted offset and bitmap bytes remain covered by the wire-image rule.
Type-width helpers preserve fixed layouts and accepted variable estimates without collapsing Date and NewDate.
Chunk codec encode and decode preserve the accepted wire image, column shapes, nulls, offsets, checked framing, and legal suffix.
cell-to-datum dispatch preserves range sentinels, float32 normalization, datum collation, raw byte families, exact numeric and temporal ordering, vector ordering, and KindRaw default equality
field-type dispatch, unsigned routing, NULL-first ordering, collation, numeric, temporal, JSON, BIT, name-value, vector and unsupported-type behavior match the accepted comparator authority
LowerBound returns the first not-less row and reports equality across duplicates, NULL prefixes, sentinels, out-of-range probes and collated strings
UpperBound returns the first strictly greater row across duplicates, NULL prefixes, sentinels, out-of-range probes and collated strings
Chunk preserves construction, state, selection, append, transform, identity and lifecycle semantics
whole-chunk reads require the exact recorded byte extent, propagate I/O failure, and never mutate a Fill destination from partial data
empty input and real storage initialization or write failures return promptly without publishing partial chunk, row, byte, file-path, or tracker state
disk counters and tracker authority publish written bytes, retain quota-exceeded accounting until close, then release bytes and the spill file exactly once
whole-chunk spill preserves native format, physical values, auxiliary state, random access, Get and Fill behavior, counters, and owner state
selection metadata round-trips and a no-selection image preserves the accepted caller-owned Fill destination selection
zero-column virtual chunks preserve capacity, required rows, virtual rows, selection, logical row count, serialization, readback, and cleanup
global capacity buckets create on first get or put, reuse on later access, remain synchronized and never cross initial capacities
list construction, row pointers, append/add routing, allocation and reuse preserve row order and chunk boundaries
GetChunk exposes the live stored chunk and Rust makes mutation authority explicit through an exclusive list borrow
memory accounting deliberately lags the writable tail, reset charges and recycles it, allocation releases its charge, and clear returns to zero
Walk visits rows in chunk order, handles an empty list, and stops at the first callback error
Pool initializes synchronized physical-width buckets, constructs empty and populated chunks, resets returned columns, preserves reachable var/4/8/40 widths and publishes each aliased owner once
packed fixed and variable cells append the intended payload and return the advanced native offset
Chunk text preserves logical row order, accepted separators, newlines and arbitrary source bytes
an in-memory row remains live without occupying disk scratch, a spilled row appends exactly once, and a stored spill error leaves scratch unchanged
a reader scans exactly the chunk extent captured at construction and never consumes a later append
the reader preserves row order, latched errors, stable end and close semantics, and remains valid while a shallow handle spills
fixed and variable selected-column copies preserve order, nulls, expected-result polarity and row-id remapping
column swapping merges input alias classes, preserves one live output owner and publishes its mapping safely under concurrent first use
direct and same-outer join copies preserve selected rows, virtual counts, empty behavior and atomic selection errors
the spill-file adapter preserves exact logical writes, cached positional reads, plaintext and AES behavior, offsets and cleanup

Rust preserves TiDB's bounded allocator and physical-width pool behavior through ownership-safe leases; Go pointer invalidation, sync.Pool GC eviction, and benchmark timing are intentionally not reproduced.
Rust preserves every typed comparison contract; Go's opaque KindInterface is intentionally excluded rather than adding an untyped GoAny box.

Rust preserves the observable Add and read failure contracts through deterministic filesystem and checksum-boundary errors; Go failpoint callback, RNG thresholds, and sleep timing are intentionally not reproduced.
The Rust List preserves TiDB's observable row storage, live chunk access, memory-accounting, reuse, and walk behavior; Go benchmark machinery is intentionally not reproduced.

Rust deterministically preserves the append, access, batch, grow/reset and memory results exercised by the accepted benchmarks; Go testing.B iteration, allocation reporting, timers, sub-benchmark names and anti-optimization output are intentionally not reproduced.

Rust deterministically preserves selected-row order, values, null behavior and virtual-row counts exercised by the accepted chunk-util benchmarks; Go testing.B iteration, timers and allocation reports are intentionally not reproduced.

The Rust reader preserves TiDB's observable row, error, extent, close, and concurrent-spill behavior; Go goroutine, channel, finalizer, and benchmark timing machinery has no independent package contract and is intentionally not reproduced.

The listed zero-iteration branches cannot execute because each accepted test loop is bound to a fixed positive literal, a positive cache limit plus ten, or a statically nonempty field/column collection populated earlier in the same test.

Safe Rust methods cannot be invoked through a nil Chunk reference, accepted FieldType.EvalType always returns one of the handled evaluation classes, and ETReal arises only from FLOAT or DOUBLE; the four listed branches therefore have no typed Rust or accepted valid-input entry path.

The listed branches have no valid accepted public entry: deserializeSel is called only for a nonzero native-int-sized selection; the same private scratch buffer serialized every stored chunk and therefore has sufficient capacity to read any of them; a successful io.ReadFull returns the requested count; and the direct source test binds all listed loops to fixed positive chunk, row, or selection counts.
The three zero-iteration branches cannot execute because TestList binds each loop to the fixed positive literal five; the Rust boundary executes the same positive-loop semantics.
No valid FieldType can route Pool.GetChunk or Pool.PutChunk to width 16 or outside the declared cases: accepted getFixedLen returns only VarElemLen, 4, 8, or 40 and Time is eight bytes.

Every listed zero-iteration arm belongs to a normal source test/helper whose accepted call binds the loop to a fixed positive row, column, selection, or all-types count. No accepted entry reaches the zero arm.
The listed loop-zero and checksum-absent arms are dominated by accepted production guards or the successful spill-file initialization invariant.
The accepted normal tests bind their source and selection loops to 1,024 rows with a positive selected subset, and valid copy inputs cannot enter their explicit failure arms.
These zero-iteration branches cannot execute because the accepted tests use fixed positive chunk and row counts; the Rust tests preserve the corresponding positive-loop semantics.
Row preserves sentinel and chunk identity, logical-to-physical indexing, typed access and datum conversion across field families
Row copy construction returns one independently owned row selected from the source
Row text preserves NULL, every reachable eval family, accepted separators and arbitrary source bytes
